title: Inference proxy
description: The per-tenant policy-enforcing proxy in front of every model call: request/response gates, egress DLP rules, and device-authorization approvals.

config.title: Gates & ceilings
config.intro: Each gate is enforced on the request path before the model call. Turning one off stops enforcing that check; the change is recorded in the audit ledger.
config.failOpenHint: When the proxy cannot reach a policy decision, allow the call instead of blocking it. Off = fail closed.
config.recordMandatoryHint: Refuse a call that cannot be recorded to the session ledger.

gatesHint.gate_model_access: Enforce which models each subject may call.
gatesHint.gate_budget: Enforce budget ceilings before the call accrues cost.
gatesHint.gate_dlp_request: Scan the outbound request for disallowed classifications.
gatesHint.gate_dlp_response: Scan the model response per the response-DLP mode.

config.responseDlpModeHint: How the response DLP handles a match: off (no scan), flag (annotate), or buffer (hold for scan before returning).
config.ceilingsEnforceHint: Cap per-call tokens, tool uses and task budget. Off = no per-call cap.

dlp.title: Egress DLP rules
dlp.intro: Map a content classification to allow or deny on egress. Classification runs server-side at the model call; these rules decide what a match does.
dlp.truncated: Loaded {{n}} DLP rules; there are more
dlp.truncatedHint: There are more DLP rules than shown; this page takes rows by id. A rule missing from this list does not prove it does not exist — egress may be governed by rules you cannot see here.
dlp.noRead: You do not have permission to view DLP rules.
dlp.emptyHint: Add a rule to allow or deny a classification on egress.

deleteDialog.title: Delete DLP rule?
deleteDialog.description: This removes the egress rule for “{{class}}”. Matching content will fall back to the default handling.

dialog.title: Add DLP rule
dialog.subtitle: A classification is allowed or denied on egress. The rule is keyed by its classification.
dialog.classHint: The content classification this rule applies to (e.g. pii, secret).

device.title: Device authorization
device.intro: Approve or deny a device-authorization request by its user code (the code shown on the device pairing screen).
device.notFound: No pending request for that user code.
device.expired: That request has expired or was already used.
